reason_en: One of the seven pooled studies is clinical surveillance indexed by visit code rather than experimental infection.
The entity is a class: different primary tumours are pooled, and one comparison contrasts tumour stages rather than disease against normal tissue.
Two of the four pooled studies administer IL-1 beta, one of them combined with IFN-gamma, rather than IL-1 alpha.
A single study contributes both nasal epithelium and peripheral blood to the same asthma-versus-normal comparison.
Two of four comparisons are mispaired: one treats absence of IL-10 as the treated arm, the other changes differentiation state together with treatment.
One study measures R5020 combined with IFN-alpha against a double vehicle, while the others measure IFN-alpha alone.
Patient tissue and immortalised cell lines are pooled, and one comparison uses the same tumour line as its own normal control.
The entity is an umbrella class: a nephrotoxicant, a chemical exposure and CD8+ T-cell antigen stimulation are pooled under a single label.
One comparison is referenced against a bortezomib vehicle instead of the vehicle used by its twin comparison in the same study.
Pituitary and colonic adenoma are pooled, and the anatomical site of a third study cannot be determined from its labels.
In one of the three pooled studies the label denotes infective third-stage nematode larvae, not the interleukin.
